newsitem.title: USA: Coleman in patent suit, sees fourth quarter affected.
newsitem.headline: Coleman in patent suit, sees fourth quarter affected.

text.p: Coleman Co. Inc., reporting a loss for the third quarter, said Wednesday that its fourth-quarter results may be affected because of litigation that Black & Decker Corp. has initiated.

Coleman said Black & Decker, the maker of household tools and appliances, last week began litigation against it and other companies, alleging infringement on a newly issued patent for certain lighting products.

Coleman, known for its own lighting products, camping stoves and other outdoor equipment, said it suspended customer shipments of its coil flashlights while it assesses the validity of the Black & Decker patent.
Coleman said the litigation might result in a five cent to 10 cent per share "negative effect on net earnings" in the fourth quarter.

Also on Wednesday, Coleman reported a third-quarter loss of $48.4 million, or 91 cents per share, compared with a profit of $8.7 million, or 16 cents per share, for the year-ago quarter. The 1996 quarter included $44.5 million in after-tax charges for restructuring and other purposes.
Revenues for the latest quarter rose to $269.6 million from $211.8 million a year earlier.
The company said the balance of the charges and any additional charges from the coil flashlight issue would be taken in the fourth quarter.
Aside from these items, the company said, "We expect to conclude the year with increased revenues and earnings in line with our historic pattern."
Coleman's stock was unchanged $14.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
